Bruno 25,000 sh @ $4.38 = $109,500; CFO Mirlanda Gecaj 10,000 sh @ $4.41 = $44,100; director Scott Letier 25,000 sh @ $4.43 = $110,750. rfm_tuples.interpretation: STRONG honest-insider commitment signal. The C-suite triumvirate (CEO, CFO, COO) plus a director put personal cash to work near the lows in May-Aug 2025. CEO Bandrowczak's purchase at $4.48 was at the all-time-low end of XRX history. This is exactly the LONG-tier Form 4 evidence the framework looks for: code-P, clustered, by C-suite, into the drawdown, with ZERO offsetting sales. The buys do NOT precede positive news — Q3 brought further dividend cuts and Q4 brought the brand-IP financing. Management was wrong about timing the bottom (stock is now at -54.8%), but they were not selling into bad news.

Combined with XRX-01, this is asymmetric P:S = infinite (zero sales). NOT the IONQ pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note: 'During the first quarter of 2025, the annual cash dividend on common stock was reduced to $0.50 per share from $1.00 per share... In the second quarter of 2025, the annual cash dividend on common stock was further reduced to $0.10 per share from $0.50 per share.'
rfm_tuples.f: Verify two-stage dividend cut against announcements; assess capital-allocation framing in narrative.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CONFIRMED: $1.00 -> $0.50 -> $0.10 annualized, a 90% cumulative cut over two consecutive quarters in 2025. Capped-call conversion-price ratchet from $27.51 down to $20.84 was triggered by these cuts. 10-K narrative reframes this as 'Reduction of debt is our primary capital allocation priority' but does not explicitly enumerate that this is a 90% dividend reduction in a single year.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two-stage dividend cut within six months is highly atypical for a former dividend-aristocrat-style cash cow like Xerox. The framing in the FY2025 10-K is muted — they spend more ink on the Lexmark synergy story than on the dividend trajectory. Severe disclosure-under-emphasis, but the cut itself is honestly recorded. Not a fraud finding — a distress finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 26 Subsequent Events: 'On February 17, 2026... Xerox Corporation contributed... the trademarks in respect of the Xerox brand (collectively, the Contributed IP), to IPCo Holdings... in exchange for $405 million aggregate principal amount of senior secured term loans... Term Loans bear interest at a per annum rate equal to either (a) a base rate plus a margin of 7.125% for ABR Loans, or (b) the applicable term SOFR rate plus a margin of 8.125% for SOFR Loans... The Licensees are required to pay IPCo a royalty fee equal to 2.0% of specified consolidated revenue generated by Holdings and its subsidiaries from the Contributed IP.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the issuer characterizes this as a 'joint venture' framed as opportunistic capital structure work, verify what the structure actually is: who controls IPCo, what is the effective cost, what are the cross-default and covenant implications.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 10-Q confirms Xerox Corporation BEGAN CONSOLIDATING IPCo Holdings as a VIE in Q1 2026 (i.e., Xerox is the primary beneficiary; IPCo carries $902M assets / $452M liabilities at 3/31/26). Effective economics: $405M senior secured term loan + $45M Class A units sold to TPG/Angelo Gordon for $405M cash distribution to parent (less $42M of fees = $363M net), against the encumbrance of the entire Xerox brand trademark portfolio worldwide. Interest cost SOFR+8.125% (i.e., ~13.5% at current SOFR) plus 4.5% quarterly amortization plus 2.0% revenue royalty paid into a reserve account. TPG/Angelo Gordon is a distressed-credit specialist; this structure (brand-IP holdco, SOFR+8.125%, revenue royalty, reserve account) is a textbook distressed-financing template (cf. Revlon 2020, J. Crew, Neiman Marcus 2018-2019 brand-IP boxes). 10-K does not enumerate the effective all-in cost or characterize it as distress finance.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: the disclosure is technically complete but the narrative framing ('joint venture arrangement', 'opportunistically addressing capital structure') understates that this is a distressed brand-IP financing at ~13.5% gross cost secured by the most valuable intangible asset Xerox owns. The 7.125%/8.125% spreads above SOFR/ABR are far above the cost of the existing 5.5% senior unsecured 2028 notes — i.e., Xerox could not refinance through conventional channels at acceptable terms. This is the single most important signal in the filing that the company's debt stack is approaching the limits of what unsecured markets will absorb.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 26: 'In January 2026 the Board of Directors approved a pro-rata distribution of warrants... On February 12, 2026, 77,271,234 warrants were issued and distributed, at no cost... Each warrant entitles the holder to purchase one share of Common Stock at an exercise price of $8.00 per share... and may be exercised (a) for cash... and (b) using designated outstanding Xerox debt securities (the Designated Notes).'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — interpret the dual-currency (cash OR existing debt) exercise feature as a structural debt-management tool.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 77.27M warrants struck at $8.00, exercisable IN CASH OR IN DEBT, with the company having sole discretion to designate which debt series are 'Designated Notes.' If exercised in debt, this gives Xerox a discretionary tool to retire face-value debt with new equity at a fixed $8 strike — effectively a forced exchange offer at management's option. Common stock currently trades ~$3 (implied from -54.8% drawdown vs ~2024 levels). Warrants are deeply out-of-the-money but have 2-year life and can expire early if VWAP >= 100% of strike for 20 of 30 trading days. The dual-currency feature is highly unusual for a stock-dividend warrant.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: this is a contingent debt-for-equity exchange dressed up as a warrant dividend. It signals (a) management explicitly anticipates the equity may need to be the currency to retire debt, and (b) they want a pre-built mechanism to do so without needing a fresh consent solicitation. Honest disclosure but ominous structural implication consistent with the IP-financing-at-distress-pricing theme.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Financial Overview: 'Total revenue of $7.0 billion in 2025 increased 12.9% reflecting a 15.5-percentage point benefit and 6.5-percentage point benefit from the Lexmark Acquisition and ITsavvy, respectively.'

Q1 2026 10-Q is more revealing: 'On a pro forma basis total revenue declined 3.7%... post sale revenue declined 3.8%.' I.e., even INCLUDING Lexmark in both periods, the combined business is shrinking ~4% YoY in Q1 2026.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: headline +12.9% revenue growth obscures continuing -8% organic Print decline. The Lexmark deal is now being used to mask, not reverse, the secular trend. Q1 2026 pro-forma -3.7% (with Lexmark in both periods) is the cleanest read and confirms the combined entity is still in decline. Disclosure is technically present in the segment tables but the narrative emphasis is entirely on Lexmark-driven optical growth.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Net (loss) for 2025 was $(1,029) million... primarily reflects higher Income tax expense, as a result of the establishment of valuation allowances of $537 million against certain deferred tax assets to reflect their realizability.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A verify reported loss; Mode B interpret the DTA valuation allowance.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CONFIRMED: $(1,029)M net loss FY2025; FY2024 $(1,321)M (which itself included $(1,058)M pre-tax goodwill impairment). Two consecutive years of >$1B GAAP losses. The $537M deferred-tax-asset valuation allowance is the auditor/management conclusion that it is no longer more-likely-than-not that Xerox will generate enough taxable income in the relevant jurisdictions to use these DTAs — i.e., management's own internal forecast no longer supports recovery of the tax-loss-carryforward asset.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A $537M DTA valuation allowance is an extremely strong forward-looking negative signal because it is management's OWN admission that future taxable income is unlikely. Combined with two consecutive billion-dollar GAAP losses, this is a severe distress indicator. The disclosure is honest — they recorded it — but the narrative consistently emphasizes adjusted (non-GAAP) profitability and never highlights the DTA writedown as a forward signal.

rfm_tuples.R: Filing chronology: Form NT 10-K filed 2026-03-02 (notification of inability to timely file); 10-K filed 2026-03-17 (15 days late vs typical Feb pattern; prior year 10-K filed 2025-02-24).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — determine reason for late filing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: NT 10-K filed 2026-03-02 indicates inability to file 10-K by the original due date (Feb 27, 2026). 10-K was ultimately filed 2026-03-17, ~18 days after original due date. The 10-K narrative does not explicitly tie the delay to any restatement or material weakness — ICFR is asserted EFFECTIVE as of 12/31/2025. The most plausible drivers given the document content: (a) Lexmark purchase accounting was still being trued up — the 10-K explicitly notes 'identified errors' in Lexmark preliminary purchase accounting with $28M goodwill increase from error correction plus $11M from measurement-period adjustments; (b) the TPG brand-IP JV closed 2026-02-17, just 10 days before the original due date, triggering subsequent-events and VIE consolidation analysis.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Late filing combined with Lexmark purchase-accounting error correction is a soft amber flag. The error correction itself is disclosed as immaterial ($28M goodwill adjustment on a multi-billion-dollar deal). However, the FY2026 10-K is the FIRST year of consolidated Lexmark + brand-IP-JV reporting, so the audit-attestation surface area is materially larger and 18 days is not egregious. ICFR opinion remains clean.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Strengthen the Balance Sheet: Reduction of debt is our primary capital allocation priority. We target a leverage ratio of less than 3.0x total debt to EBITDA.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A verify the leverage target against actual leverage at YE 2025; Mode B test the path to <3.0x.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K balance sheet) + cross-check with adj EBITDA
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt $4.2B at 12/31/2025 ($2.5B unsecured + $1.7B secured), of which ~$1.5B is allocated to financing business (7:1 lev on $1.7B finance assets). 2025 Adjusted Net Loss $(62)M; reported GAAP Net Loss $(1,029)M. Reverse-engineering EBITDA: amortization of intangible assets is materially higher post-Lexmark, depreciation $100M in Q1 alone annualized ~$400M, plus restructuring add-backs. Even generous adj EBITDA of ~$700-800M against $4.2B total debt = 5.3-6.0x, or against $2.7B 'non-financing' debt = 3.4-3.9x. NEITHER metric currently meets the <3.0x target. Then the Feb 2026 IPCo financing ADDED $405M of new senior secured debt at SOFR+8.125%. Operating cash flow guide CUT in Q1 10-Q from $360M to $350M due to higher JV interest expense.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The stated <3.0x leverage target is aspirational, not current. Actual leverage is 3.4-6.0x depending on whether you include financing debt and which EBITDA measure. The most recent capital action (TPG IP JV) ADDED debt at distressed pricing. Operating cash flow guide was reduced because of the new interest cost. This is the inverse of the stated capital-allocation priority — Xerox is currently LEVERING UP at very expensive cost rather than de-levering. Severe gap between R and M.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'The Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared on a going concern basis... we are not aware of any other trends or demands, commitments, events or uncertainties that will result in or that are reasonably likely to result in our liquidity increasing or decreasing in any material way that will impact our capital needs during or beyond the next [12 months].' Auditor opinion: 'We maintained effective internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) as of December 31, 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify there is no going-concern qualification and no material weakness.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CONFIRMED: No going-concern qualification. No material weakness identified — ICFR opinion is unqualified for both Xerox Holdings and Xerox Corporation. 'Material weakness' appears 6 times in the 10-K only in risk-factor and policy-narrative language, never as an identified finding. Auditor (PwC) issued clean attestation. Critical audit matters likely include Lexmark purchase-price allocation and goodwill recoverability (Print & Other reporting unit, $2.2B goodwill at YE25).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Despite the distress signals (dividend cut, DTA write-off, brand-IP financing, two-year ~$2.4B cumulative losses), the auditor has NOT qualified going concern and ICFR is clean. This bounds the worst case: the company has at least 12-month liquidity per management/PwC's assessment as of 12/31/2025, supported by ABL availability, $363M net IPCo proceeds, and the option to monetize the $1.7B finance receivable portfolio.

summary: XRX is a paradox: severe operational/structural distress signals (90% dividend cut in 2025, two consecutive billion-dollar GAAP net losses, $537M DTA valuation allowance, Feb-2026 brand-IP financing with TPG/Angelo Gordon at SOFR+8.125% secured by the Xerox trademark, secular print decline still ~-4% YoY on pro forma) directly contradicted by an unusually clean Form 4 tape — six open-market PURCHASES totaling $502K by the CEO (Bandrowczak), CFO (Gecaj), COO (Bruno), and a director (Letier) over 24 months, ZERO open-market sales, at prices ($3.95-4.48) at/near the all-time low. Disclosure quality is honest; the issuer records the bad news (dividend cut, DTA writedown, IP-JV, warrant dividend with debt-for-equity option) without obfuscation, but the narrative framing under-emphasizes how distressed the brand-IP financing actually is. The framework's honesty-alpha logic does NOT short XRX: management is committing personal capital alongside shareholders and the going-concern + ICFR opinions are clean. However, the structural distress (leverage 3.4-6x vs <3.0x target; brand-IP pledged) is severe enough that this is NOT a clean LONG either. Verdict: NEUTRAL with LONG-tier insider tape — honest disclosure of distress, with the insider buying being the strongest contrarian indicator.
verdict_tier_form4_only: LONG (clean insider tape: CEO/CFO/COO purchases, zero sales, $502K total)
verdict_tier_fundamentals_only: SHORT (90% dividend cut, $1B annual losses, $537M DTA writedown, brand-IP at distress pricing, organic revenue still declining)
